h1: Dog Years to Human Years Calculator (by Size)
description: Convert your dog's age to human years instantly. Uses the AAHA size-adjusted formula — not the outdated "×7" rule. Includes a conversion chart for small, medium, large, and giant breeds.
answerSnippet: A 3-year-old medium dog equals about 34 human years. The "×7" rule is wrong — dogs age 15 human years in year 1, add 9 in year 2, then +4–7/year depending on size (AAHA method): small breeds add 4/year, medium 5/year, large 6/year, and giant breeds 7/year.
intro: The old "multiply by 7" rule is a myth. Dogs age 15 human years in their first year alone, then 9 more in year 2 — and after that, the rate depends on breed size. Large dogs age faster and have shorter lifespans than small dogs. This calculator uses the AAHA/AKC size-adjusted method, the current veterinary standard. Just enter your dog's age and size to get the correct human-year equivalent and life stage.
keyTakeaway: **AAHA size-adjusted formula:** Year 1 = 15 human years · Year 2 adds 9 (total 24) · Each additional year: +4 (small) / +5 (medium) / +6 (large) / +7 (giant). A 5-year-old large dog = 42 human years; a 5-year-old small dog = 36 human years.

fields.helpText: Size is the main factor in how dogs age. Large and giant breeds age faster and have shorter lifespans.

explanation:
## Why the '×7 Rule' Is Wrong

The old rule of multiplying a dog's age by 7 was never based on science — it was a rough average invented for simplicity. Dogs age far more rapidly in their first two years, and the rate differs significantly by breed size.

## The AAHA Size-Adjusted Formula

The American Animal Hospital Association (AAHA) 2019 Canine Life Stage Guidelines define the current standard:

- **Year 1**: 15 human years
- **Year 2**: +9 human years (total = 24)
- **Each additional year** varies by size:
  - Small (< 10 kg): +4 human years/year
  - Medium (10–25 kg): +5 human years/year
  - Large (25–45 kg): +6 human years/year
  - Giant (> 45 kg): +7 human years/year

## Dog Age Conversion Chart by Size

| Dog Age | Small (< 10 kg) | Medium (10–25 kg) | Large (25–45 kg) | Giant (> 45 kg) |
|---------|----------------|-------------------|-----------------|----------------|
| 1 year  | 15             | 15                | 15              | 15             |
| 2 years | 24             | 24                | 24              | 24             |
| 3 years | 28             | 29                | 30              | 31             |
| 4 years | 32             | 34                | 36              | 38             |
| 5 years | 36             | 39                | 42              | 45             |
| 6 years | 40             | 44                | 48              | 52             |
| 7 years | 44             | 49                | 54              | 59             |
| 8 years | 48             | 54                | 60              | 66             |
| 9 years | 52             | 59                | 66              | 73             |
| 10 years | 56            | 64                | 72              | 80             |
| 12 years | 64            | 74                | 84              | 94             |
| 15 years | 76            | 89                | 102             | 115            |

## Life Stages by Size

| Stage | Small | Medium | Large | Giant |
|-------|-------|--------|-------|-------|
| Puppy | < 1 yr | < 1 yr | < 1 yr | < 1 yr |
| Young adult | 1–3 yrs | 1–3 yrs | 1–3 yrs | 1–3 yrs |
| Mature adult | 3–11 yrs | 3–9 yrs | 3–8 yrs | 3–6 yrs |
| Senior | 11+ yrs | 9+ yrs | 8+ yrs | 6+ yrs |

Knowing your dog's life stage helps you schedule the right veterinary checkups, adjust nutrition, and monitor for age-related health changes.

## Why Large Dogs Age Faster

Larger dogs produce more growth hormone and have faster metabolic processes that lead to earlier cell aging. A Great Dane at age 6 is already in senior territory; a Chihuahua at 6 is still a mature adult with many active years ahead.

faq.q: How do you convert dog years to human years?
faq.a: The accurate method (AAHA standard): Year 1 = 15 human years, Year 2 adds 9 (total 24), then add 4–7 human years per dog year depending on size. Small dogs add 4/year, medium 5/year, large 6/year, giant breeds 7/year. The old ×7 rule is inaccurate.

faq.q: How old is a 7-year-old dog in human years?
faq.a: It depends on size. A 7-year-old small dog ≈ 44 human years; medium ≈ 49; large ≈ 54; giant ≈ 59. The common answer of '49 years' only applies to medium breeds.

faq.q: At what age is a dog considered senior?
faq.a: Small breeds become senior around 11 years old, medium breeds at 9, large breeds at 8, and giant breeds as early as 6 years old. Senior dogs benefit from twice-yearly vet visits and adjusted nutrition.

faq.q: Is my 2-year-old dog really like a 24-year-old human?
faq.a: Yes — according to veterinary standards, a 2-year-old dog has already gone through the equivalent of 24 human years of development. They are fully sexually mature, physically adult, but still young adults behaviorally.

faq.q: Why do small dogs live longer than large dogs?
faq.a: Larger dogs have accelerated growth rates and higher insulin-like growth factor levels, which speed up cellular aging. A Great Dane's median lifespan is around 8–10 years; a Chihuahua's is 15–17 years.

faq.q: How old is a 3-month-old puppy in human years?
faq.a: A 3-month-old (0.25 years) puppy is roughly equivalent to 3–4 human years — developmentally similar to a toddler. By 6 months they are closer to 10 human years, going through adolescence.

faq.q: Is the AAHA formula better than the NIA/UCSD epigenetic clock method?
faq.a: Both are improvements over ×7. The UCSD epigenetic clock (2020) is based on DNA methylation and gives a more biological conversion, but is complex to apply manually. The AAHA size-adjusted formula is the practical veterinary standard for daily use and is what this calculator applies.

faq.q: Does breed (not just size) affect dog aging?
faq.a: Yes, individual breeds show some variation beyond size, but size is by far the strongest predictor. The AAHA formula uses size categories because that's the most reliable variable for population-level aging estimates.

faq.q: What size category is a Labrador Retriever?
faq.a: Labradors typically weigh 25–36 kg (55–80 lb), placing them in the large category. A 5-year-old Labrador = approximately 42 human years under this formula.
